title: PS5 And Xbox Series X|S Console Sales Surged Just Before GTA 6 Came Out
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and to play the game natively, you need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Unsurprisingly, new data shows that PlayStation and Xbox console sales surged in the week before release. According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there was a "significant surge" in hardware sales in the US for the week that ended November 14. PS5 sales were >2.4x the same week last year, while Xbox Series X|S sales increased by >2.3x. GTA 6 is not available on Switch 2, but that console saw a 40% surge in sales compared to the same week in 2025. Before launch, Piscatella said GTA 6 should help boost PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales, but maybe not so dramatically due to the astronomical cost of a new console. To help save money, you could buy an Xbox One and stream GTA 6. Alternatively, people have discovered that you can stream the game to a PlayStation Portal device. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

title: Is GTA 6 Too Easy? Rockstar Weighs In
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking about is the game's difficulty level. Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that Rockstar's data showed that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA 5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in the middle." GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That said, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder. Design producer Scott Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel "appropriate." “We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained. Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much. "There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so big, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that, making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth into as well.” GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

title: Witcher 4 Won’t Be A PS5 Exclusive After New Deal With PlayStation
description: CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing deal for The Witcher 4, but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to PlayStation. CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski said on social media, "Just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform." The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a number of ways in the marketing campaign. Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red is making Cyberpunk 2, a new IP codenamed Hadar, a new game believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher title, and a remake of the original Witcher. On the mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't been announced yet. The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it, and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4 likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in January 2028. That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4 will have some kind of physical goodies for fans. In other news about The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red recently discussed the game in comparison to GTA 6. "Of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4–I think so, yes," Nowakowski said. "It’s been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.”

title: GTA 6’s Fake Tunnel Is A Great Way To Turn Your Muscle Car Into Scrap Metal
description: GTA 6 has no shortage of forces trying to put a damper on your crime spree, but the long arm of the law might be the least of your worries if you're planning a successful caper in Vice City. As players have discovered, the greatest threat to a clean getaway might just be an impressive mural, as they've smashed their vehicles right into an unforgiving wall that looks like it was ripped straight out of a Road Runner cartoon. Located in Vice City's Decor District, this piece of street art resembles a tunnel going under the nearby overpass, and at high speed, it's pretty convincing--something I discovered to my dismay, totaling my pretty sweet muscle car in the process. Does anyone have an industrial-strength magnet so that I can start working out these dents? I'm sure it'll buff out. It's a delicious bit of trolling from Rockstar Games: the kind of design choice that would make Looney Tunes legend Tex Avery proud with how effective it is. Numerous players have been caught out, and this is just one of many little secrets and Easter eggs hidden in the game. Fortunately, a gas station was nearby, and my muscle car limped to it for a quick repair. In case you want to wreck your car, visit this location in the Decor District of Vice City. As GTA 6 prepares to celebrate its first record-breaking week of release, players have made plenty of discoveries. The Bigfoot mystery has been solved, you can hop into a portal to visit Vice City during the '80s, and there's even an island where bored rich people will hunt you. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: GTA 6 Modders Are Trying To Vibe-Code A PC Port, And It’s Not Going Well
description: PC modders are racing to get GTA 6 playable on PC after the leak of the game's complete Xbox build, but so far it doesn't look too promising. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games haven't been sitting idle either, as one of the leads behind the Project Leonida Discord group claimed in now-deleted social media posts that they were stepping away from the mammoth task of getting GTA 6 to run on PC. Project Leonida has also been taken down, but it's not the only group trying to get GTA 6 running outside of PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. None of these groups have succeeded yet, and as Twitter user Chasm detailed online, maybe relying heavily on AI tools isn't the way to go. Dev streams have been full of users leveraging generative AI tools to do something, with several prompts being absolute gems of wishful thinking. Here's a snippet of what people have been throwing at Google's Antigravity, while butchering the English language: Continue working and do apply ever part of the code make no mistakes You need todo one thing at a time not a little bit of everything we need all the game start like the rockstar launch so on that stuff, not in game stuff yet work faster there has to be a faster way to iterate than this Even with an army of enthusiasts throwing prompts and cash at generative AI, a copied version of GTA 6 still seems far out of reach. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick commented in March that the idea of using AI and simply pushing a button to make a hit game was "laughable," and he referenced the music industry, which is grappling with a flood of AI slop to top streaming platforms. "Right now [in music] there are programs that allow you to put out a prompt and get a professionally recorded song spit back out at you. It sounds like a song, but I defy you to listen to it more than once. It's great to send as a greeting card to your partner on their birthday, but that's about it," Zelnick said. Whatever progress is made in the GTA 6 PC port scene,…

title: Even Max Verstappen has succumbed to GTA 6 fever, squeezing in 40 hours around his Las Vegas Grand Prix win
The Witcher 4 Wants To Be The GTA 6 Of The Witcher Franchise
description: There's been a massive gap between new entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4, developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio says it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4. "First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer ). "But I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4." When The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt was first released in 2015, it was hailed for raising the bar for open-world adventure games. Its side-quests were singled out for being narratively dense, full of micro-consequences, and on par with the main campaign missions. In the years since, numerous open-world games have used The Witcher 3 as a blueprint, with notable examples being the Assassin's Creed trilogy of Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla alongside Sony's Horizon Zero Dawn and Ghost of Tsushima. Eleven years later, that bar has been raised again with GTA 6, which offers emergent, player-driven open-world chaos through multiple systems. The world of The Witcher is naturally very different from the consumerism-focused setting of GTA 6, but if The Witcher 4 builds on its predecessor's strengths and adds more nuance to those gameplay mechanics, we…

title: Death Stranding 2 Made Me Bawl Like A Baby, And My GOTY Is Now Cheaper Than Ever
description: As a parent, Death Stranding 2: On The Beach may be one of the most gut-wrenching, devastating pieces of media that I’ve ever had the pleasure of experiencing. On the surface, it seems like a delivery game that sees you acting as a courier in a post-apocalyptic world. That is true, but it’s also a beautifully chaotic game that you should buy now that it's at a lower price than ever. Especially if you played the first one. At its core, Death Stranding 2 is a familiar Kojima experience: weird gameplay mechanics that few directors would ever attempt, mixed with an emotional narrative that somehow delicately balances being absolutely crazy and serious. Once again filling the well-worn shoes of Sam Porter Bridges, this time you're not reconnecting America—you're reconnecting Australia, following an incident that left me with tears in my eyes and a lump in my throat. While the first game leaned more heavily into the delivery aspect, Death Stranding 2 pushes into more action-oriented situations. It feels like Metal Gear Solid, but with Norman Reedus front and center, using blood-filled grenades against spooky black cloud monsters. That is a factual statement, and if you don’t believe me, you can play it yourself. While BTs, the aforementioned spooky black cloud things, are one of the major enemy types, there are other, less-supernatural enemies to blast your guns at—from the cargo-stealing MULEs to the robotic samurai called Ghost Mechs. Even with combat having more of a presence in the sequel, Death Stranding 2 is far from an action game. The moments that are truly special remain the journeys from Point A to Point B, and occasionally, a side trip to Point C. Delivering requires plenty of planning, loading your cargo in the right way for a long trip that will see you go off the network, meaning you’ll be on your own. Inside the network, other versions of Sam (so, other players) may have left some stuff to help you get across the world, making you feel connected despite…

title: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
description: At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason. Read more

They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "new heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day. Read more
